source.document: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
source.normalized_statement: There exists a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite finite simple graphs, every member containing a cycle, such that ex(n,F)=O(n^(4/3-1/48)) while for every member H of F one has ex(n,H)=Omega(n^(4/3)). Consequently no member controls the family extremal number up to a constant factor, so the corrected Erdos-Simonovits compactness conjecture fails.

definition_concordance.analysis: Mathlib SimpleGraph is loopless and symmetric, and the Fin vertex type makes each stored graph finite with an explicit order.

definition_concordance.lean_encoding: FamilyFree family host := forall forbidden in family, forbidden.graph.Free host
definition_concordance.analysis: At the pinned mathlib revision, H.Free G is the predicate used by extremalNumber for a host G containing no copy of H; the argument order is therefore source-correct rather than reversed.

definition_concordance.lean_encoding: familyExtremal family n is the supremum of edge counts over all family-free graphs on Fin n
definition_concordance.analysis: Because the type of simple graphs on Fin n is finite, the Finset supremum is the maximum edge count in the source definition of ex(n,F).

definition_concordance.source_concept: every family member contains a cycle
definition_concordance.lean_encoding: IsCyclicFamily family := forall forbidden in family, not forbidden.graph.IsAcyclic
definition_concordance.analysis: For finite simple graphs, failure of acyclicity is exactly the existence of a cycle, matching the corrected compactness-conjecture domain.

definition_concordance.source_concept: compactness up to a constant factor
definition_concordance.lean_encoding: IsCompactFamily family := exists forbidden in family, exists C>0, eventually ex(n,forbidden) <= C*familyExtremal family n
definition_concordance.analysis: This has the source quantifier order, positive constant, selected family member, inequality direction, and sufficiently-large-n interpretation through the atTop filter.

definition_concordance.lean_encoding: CompactnessConjectureStatement quantifies over every nonempty cyclic finite family and concludes IsCompactFamily
definition_concordance.analysis: The formal statement excludes the elementary acyclic counterexamples and captures the corrected source formulation rather than the historically original version.

hypothesis_concordance.analysis: The family is intrinsically finite and theorem-level nonemptiness is explicit, so the existential cannot be discharged by the empty family.

hypothesis_concordance.lean_encoding: for every forbidden in family: Connected, IsBipartite, and not IsAcyclic
hypothesis_concordance.analysis: All three structural restrictions in source Theorem 1.1 are carried memberwise and are not weakened to a property of only one graph.

hypothesis_concordance.lean_encoding: exists c C : Real with 0<c and 0<C
hypothesis_concordance.analysis: The quantitative theorem exposes positive lower- and upper-bound constants and does not allow zero constants to make either asymptotic claim vacuous.

conclusion_concordance.lean_encoding: compactnessCounterexample_bigO uses IsBigO atTop for familyExtremal with exponent 4/3-1/48
conclusion_concordance.analysis: The asymptotic filter, exponent, direction, and family extremal function agree with the source theorem; the quantitative companion also records the equivalent power-16 bound with exponent 21.

conclusion_concordance.lean_encoding: UniformMemberLower family c gives eventually c*n^(4/3) <= extremalNumber n forbidden for every member
conclusion_concordance.analysis: The source permits constants depending on each member. Since the family is finite, a common positive minimum constant and common threshold exist, so the uniform Lean form is an equivalent finite-family strengthening.

conclusion_concordance.lean_encoding: not IsCompactFamily family and not CompactnessConjectureStatement
conclusion_concordance.analysis: The result explicitly negates both the property for the constructed family and the universal corrected conjecture, matching the source consequence.

nonvacuity.reason: The Comparator-checked existential theorems produce a nonempty finite family, positive constants, memberwise connected/bipartite/cyclic witnesses, an upper asymptotic bound, and positive lower asymptotic bounds. The theorem therefore cannot succeed from an empty family, zero constant, or empty member domain.

scope_exclusions: This audit does not certify the paper's explicit combinatorial construction separately from the already kernel-checked existential theorem.
No claim is made about alternative historical formulations of compactness outside the corrected cyclic-family statement encoded here.

disposition.reason: The formal definitions reproduce the corrected compactness conjecture, including the H-free orientation and asymptotic quantifiers. The checked existential theorem supplies all source structural properties and nonzero asymptotic witnesses, while the only apparent strengthening—a uniform lower constant—is equivalent for a finite family.
